To have a core, we need cycles (the peeling must get stuck). The endpoint-cycle example shows a cycle of 3 nodes survives.

So cores require cyclic structures! The sliding windows over a chain peel completely. That's why my earlier fuzz generators (random paths over a small node set, forming cycles) produced cores, but with high width.

So to generate low-width cores, I need cyclic structures with low treewidth. Ideas:
1. A "cycle" of nodes with paths going around it in both directions — like the endpoint-cycle example (3 nodes). For a cycle of N nodes with 3-ASN paths [v_i, v_{i+1}, v_{i+2}] for all i (mod N): let me check whether links are peripheral. Link {v_i, v_{i+1}}: contained in paths [v_{i-1}, v_i, v_{i+1}] (v_i is interior, v_{i+1} interior) — hmm: in path [v_{i-1},v_i,v_{i+1}], the endpoints are v_{i-1} and v_{i+1}; so for link {v_i,v_{i+1}}: v_i is not an endpoint, v_{i+1} IS an endpoint ✓. And in path [v_i, v_{i+1}, v_{i+2}]: endpoints v_i and v_{i+2}; v_i IS an endpoint ✓, v_{i+1} not. So for u = v_i (assuming v_i < v_{i+1}... the canonical min could be either): hmm, we need ONE fixed endpoint that is an endpoint in ALL containing paths. v_i is an endpoint in path [v_i,v_{i+1},v_{i+2}] but not in [v_{i-1},v_i,v_{i+1}]; v_{i+1} is an endpoint in the latter but not the former. So not marked ✓. So a cyclic set of paths on a cycle survives as core ✓.

The scope graph for such a structure: link l_i = {v_i, v_{i+1}} has contexts l_{i-1} and l_{i+1} → scope {l_{i-1}, l_i, l_{i+1}} → the scope graph is the square of the cycle → treewidth 2 ✓ (for N ≥ 5ish). So cycles give width 2 ✓.
